title: Roll with meat and/or shrimp, vegetables and rice paper (not fried)

content.title: About
content.content: The roll is made from thin rice paper that wraps boiled meat (beef, chicken) and/or shrimp, fresh vegetables (carrot, cucumber, bell pepper, lettuce) and sometimes rice vermicelli. It is served cold without frying, preserving the natural flavors of the ingredients and making it light and nutritious.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Rice paper is a staple in Asian cuisine, especially in Vietnamese spring rolls (gỏi).
Because the roll is not fried, it retains more heat‑sensitive vitamins, such as vitamin C from the fresh vegetables.
Shrimp used in rolls are usually pre‑boiled, making them safe to eat without additional cooking.
Meat in the roll is sliced thinly, which eases chewing and creates a pleasant texture contrast with crunchy vegetables.
Rice paper is gluten‑free, so these rolls are suitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Meat and shrimp provide complete protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The absence of frying makes the roll low‑calorie with minimal saturated fat.

items.title: Rich in vitamins and minerals
items.content: Vegetables supply vitamin C, potassium and fiber, while shrimp add iodine and selenium, important for thyroid function.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Fiber from vegetables and vermicelli promotes healthy bowel movements.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Fresh vegetables have a high water content, helping maintain fluid balance.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Shrimp can trigger severe allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: If rolls are left at room temperature too long, the risk of pathogenic bacterial growth increases.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Dipping sauces (soy sauce, fish sauce) are often high in sodium; people with hypertension should limit their use.

items.title: Additives in processed meat
items.content: If processed meat is used, be aware of possible nitrates and preservatives.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the roll cold, typically with soy sauce, peanut sauce, or sweet chili. It is eaten by hand, pulling apart the rice‑paper sheets. For extra flavor, add fresh lime juice, mint, or cilantro.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep rolls in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Before serving, ensure the rice paper has not dried out; lightly mist it with water if needed. Discard any rolls that develop a sour smell or slimy texture.
